title: Ben Thanh Market
text: Ben Thanh Market is a major landmark in central Ho Chi Minh City. It features hundreds of stalls selling local souvenirs, garments, handicrafts, and authentic Vietnamese street food.
source: Ho Chi Minh City Travel Guide 2026

title: Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon
text: Built by French colonists between 1863 and 1880, Notre-Dame Cathedral features distinct red bricks imported from Marseille and two 58-meter bell towers in Paris Square.
source: Ho Chi Minh City Travel Guide 2026

title: Saigon Central Post Office
text: Located right next to Notre-Dame Cathedral, the Saigon Central Post Office was designed with Gothic and Renaissance influences. It remains a fully functional post office.
source: Ho Chi Minh City Travel Guide 2026

title: War Remnants Museum
text: The War Remnants Museum contains exhibits relating to the Vietnam War and the First Indochina War, displaying military equipment, photographs, and historical artifacts.
source: Ho Chi Minh City Travel Guide 2026

title: Independence Palace
text: Also known as Reunification Palace, this historic site was the home and workplace of the President of South Vietnam during the Vietnam War. It features 1960s architecture and underground bunkers.
source: Ho Chi Minh City Travel Guide 2026

title: Landmark 81
text: Landmark 81 is the tallest skyscraper in Vietnam, located along the Saigon River in Binh Thanh District. It hosts a luxury mall, observation deck, hotel, and restaurants.
source: Ho Chi Minh City Travel Guide 2026

title: Bui Vien Walking Street
text: Bui Vien Walking Street is the center of nightlife in Saigon, bustling with bars, pubs, live music venues, street performances, and food stalls every evening.
source: Ho Chi Minh City Travel Guide 2026

title: Saigon Pho (Southern Style)
text: Saigon Pho features a sweeter broth compared to Northern Pho, served with flat rice noodles, fresh bean sprouts, basil, sawtooth herb, hoisin sauce, and chili sauce.
source: Ho Chi Minh City Travel Guide 2026

title: Nguyen Hue Walking Street
text: A broad pedestrian boulevard extending from City Hall to the Saigon River. It is popular for evening strolls, street buskers, pop-up events, and surrounding cafe apartments.
source: Ho Chi Minh City Travel Guide 2026

title: Cu Chi Tunnels
text: Located roughly 70 km northwest of central Saigon, the Cu Chi Tunnels are an extensive underground network used by Viet Cong soldiers during the war.
source: Ho Chi Minh City Travel Guide 2026

title: Com Tam (Broken Rice)
text: Com Tam is an iconic Saigon dish made of broken rice grains served with grilled pork chops (suon), steamed egg loaf (cha), shredded pork skin (bi), and fish sauce dip.
source: Ho Chi Minh City Travel Guide 2026

title: Jade Emperor Pagoda
text: Built in 1909 by the Chinese community, this Taoist pagoda features intricate woodcarvings, colorful statues, and incense-filled worship halls.
source: Ho Chi Minh City Travel Guide 2026
